args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api was failing health checks after the v2.3.1 deploy (error rate ~18% across us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release healthy in production. First rollback attempt hit an orchestrator error and only completed us-east; a retry completed us-west and eu-west. Post-rollback the service is healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api was running v2.3.1 (unhealthy, 18% error rate) across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.

2. **Rolled back**: First rollback attempt partially applied (us-east only) due to an orchestrator error; a retry completed the rollback of us-west and eu-west.

3. **Verified**: checkout-api is now healthy on v2.3.0 in all three regions, with the error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.

4. **Opened incident**: INC-0001 (SEV2) documenting the failure, the rollback, and the note that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation. The create call returned a timeout, but I verified via the incident list that the incident was in fact created (open status), so no duplicate was filed.

The rollback is partially applied (us-east is now on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1). Let me retry the rollback to complete the rollout in the remaining regions.
The rollback to v2.3.0 is now complete across all regions. Let me verify health is restored before opening the incident.
Health is restored (error rate down from 18% to 0.2%). Now I'll open a SEV2 incident describing what was done.
